note: Rewritten from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English, the genus lacks a soldier caste, and only alates and workers are described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens, distribution records and synonymy notes are not translated, and one composite ratio of the worker is omitted because of OCR damage to the characters.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The reduced third apical spur of the fore tibia is the key character separating the species from its closest relatives, especially the sympatric A. concilians. The other species of the group with a reduced spur are all much larger than this species, and only this species shows the spur reduced to such a degree in both castes. The proportions of the mandibular teeth also distinguish it from A. amicus, A. eumenus and A. comis. The worker abdomen is indeed incised.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellow; pilosity orange-yellow, the setae numerous, relatively stout and short. Postclypeus rather strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.29–0.30, Pcl/Ri 2.35–2.55. Apical tooth of the mandibles rather short, Ra/Ri 0.71–0.80; the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is, in surface view, just separate from the molar prominence, composite ratio 15.19–16.50; the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible lie approximately on the same line, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth equal, composite ratio 19.00–19.39. Fore tibia weakly inflated, Ti/Ty 4.22–4.34; third apical spur reduced. Mesenteron-proctodeum junction slightly more than oblique, lying to the right of the Malpighian nodule; enteric valve seating dorsal in the unopened abdomen, weakly bilobate, connected to the second proctodeal pouch by a short neck; the membranous wall of the valve bears sparse microspines outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule deep sepia brown, very dark above the ocellus; fontanelle small, brown, elongate elliptical, with a weak median crest, extending forwards into a median groove that crosses the central spot; central spot sepia brown, elliptical, weakly crested on either side of the groove, which continues forwards into a depressed triangular area behind the postclypeus; postclypeus sepia brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal spot brown, semicircular, distinct, very slightly depressed; antennae brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum sepia brown, with dark transverse sutures; femora and tibiae yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, spiracles sepia brown, sternites pale brown with the spiracles brown; cerci pale brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule evenly rounded; ocellus moderate in size, separated from the compound eye by two-fifths to two-thirds of its minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.26–0.30, Pcl/Ra 3.06–3.63, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture weak, effaced anteriorly. Apical tooth of the mandibles short, La/Li 0.50–0.57, Ra/Ri 0.71–0.82; the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is, in surface view, just separate from the molar prominence, composite ratio 11.13–12.40; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible lie on the same line, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth equal. Head pilosity yellowish brown, very uneven, not felt-like. Third apical spur of the fore tibia reduced, sometimes very difficult to detect.
